_why_these_seven: Not typos: tsc finds those and proves nothing about the gate. Each aims at a
seam where a check is plausibly weak, and each is a real bug shape that has
1 terminal guard AND its backstop removed  defence in depth defeated
2 transition table widened                 a guard that permits more
3 declined dropped from proposed           a specific edge, right on average
4 hash normalisation weakened              correct for most inputs
5 hash prefix dropped                      an output format silently changed
6 isTerminal always false                  a predicate made constant
7 health endpoint reports failure          the app boots but does not work

_the_defect_1_investigation: Defect 1 originally replaced only the isTerminal guard with `if (false)`.
Measured with lint disabled, the tests did NOT fail, and the mutation was
scored CAUGHT purely because eslint objected to unreachable code. That is
the linter having an opinion about the SHAPE of the mutation rather than
the suite noticing broken behaviour, and a real regression never arrives
So the second version removed the BACKSTOP instead: it widened the terminal
rows of the transition table. The tests still passed, and reading vitest
directly explained why. `validateJobTransition` has DEFENCE IN DEPTH: the
isTerminal guard runs first and throws before the table is ever consulted.
Neither layer alone is load-bearing, which is the correct design.
The conclusion, verified rather than assumed: there is NO coverage hole
here. tests/domain/job-validation.test.ts asserts every terminal source
against every target, ten assertions in total. The only mutation that can
make the tests fail is one that removes BOTH layers, which is what defect 1
now does. It is a legitimate mutation (a careless refactor collapsing two
checks into none) and it measures the suite rather than the linter.

defects.why: A completed or declined job could be moved again. The whole point of a terminal state is that the record stops changing, and a credential issued against a job that later moves is a lie with a signature on it.
Any status could jump to any other, so a job could reach 'completed' without a pull request ever existing. That is the exact path by which an unearned verified hire enters the record.

A specific edge rather than the whole table: a buyer could no longer decline a proposed job, so the only way out of a bad brief is to complete it. A test that only asserts the happy path never notices.

Two specs that differ only by trailing whitespace would hash differently, so the confirmed acceptance criteria would stop matching the brief the buyer actually approved. Correct for most inputs and wrong exactly where it matters.

The stored hash stops being self-describing. Every comparison still works today and nothing can ever migrate to a second algorithm, which is the kind of decision that is free to make and expensive to reverse.
A predicate made constant. Everything that asks 'is this finished?' gets no, so terminal handling is dead code everywhere at once. A gate that only exercises the happy path sees nothing.

The app boots but its health endpoint fails. If this escapes, APP_STARTED and E2E_PASSED are being printed by something that never checked whether the app answers, which would make both markers theatre.
